newsitem.title: FRANCE: YACHTING-STRICKEN SOLO RACER TAKES TO LIFE RAFT.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-STRICKEN SOLO RACER TAKES TO LIFE RAFT.

text.p: A French yachtsman in trouble in freak seas in the roaring 40s in a solo round-the-world race has boarded a life raft dumped by an Australian air force rescue plane on Thursday, race organisers said in Paris.
The Orion plane began a search for Raphael Dinelli after he set off distress signals from his 18.3 metre (60 ft) yacht Algimouss, some 1,200 nautical miles southwest of Western Australia.
A spokesman for the organisers of the Vendee Globe race said Dinelli, 28, boarded the raft on instructions from the rescue plane. He appeared to be safe but his yacht was half-submerged.
Competitors sailing in the area were re-routed to rescue Dinelli. One of them, Briton Pete Goss, was expected to reach him around 2200 GMT.

Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) spokesman David Gray earlier told reporters that Dinelli had set off distress signals early on Thursday morning as the yacht met heavy seas and winds. He was said to be out of radio contact.

French maritime officials requested assistance from Australia after picking up the distress signals. Race officials use a different international satellite navigation system to that used in Australia.
Two years ago Australian officials launched a A$1 million (US$790,000) rescue mission to save French yachtswoman Isabelle Autissier.
She was eventually winched from her dismasted yacht in an operation criticised by Australian newspapers because Australia and not race officials had to foot the bill.
